name: computer-use-x11
description: The X11 DRIVER of the computer-use@1 seam (provider id `x11`): screenshot (full screen or region), pointer (move/click/drag/scroll), keyboard (type/chords), clipboard read/write, window list/focus/close/launch/wait and screen geometry, over a headless display the driver can OWN (`target: xvfb`) or one that already exists (`target: existing`), driven either on the host (`runner: local`) or inside a container (`runner: docker`). Every capability is probed (xdpyinfo/xdotool/import/xclip/wmctrl) and every unavailable action fails with a typed error naming the missing half - never a fake success. It runs binaries, so it declares execution host.

config.description: Which display the driver drives (an existing one or an owned Xvfb), where the toolchain runs (host or a container), and the toolchain itself.

target.description: `existing`: attach to the display in `display` / $DISPLAY (nothing is started, nothing is owned). `xvfb`: the driver STARTS an Xvfb (default :99) and kills it in its disposer - the headless shape.

runner.description: `local`: the toolchain runs where the workbench process runs. `docker`: every binary runs inside `container` through `docker exec`, so the desktop is a disposable target.

display.description: The X display name, e.g. `:0` or `:99` (default: $DISPLAY; `:99` when the target is owned).

container.description: The container the `docker` runner drives (required by that runner).

xvfb.description: The geometry and extra arguments of an OWNED display.

display.description: The display name of the owned Xvfb (default :99).

args.description: Extra Xvfb arguments, handed over verbatim (argv, never a shell string).

windowManager.description: The WM started on an OWNED display, or `none`. Without a WM, window listing falls back to xdotool and focus/close are less precise (reported, never silent).

screenshotDir.description: Where screenshots are written (default: <tmpdir>/workbench-computer-use). They are captured on stdout and written by the driver, so local and docker behave identically.

typeDelayMs.description: Keystroke delay of `xdotool type` when the caller names none.

toolTimeoutMs.description: The bound of ONE tool invocation (e.g. `import -window root`). Exceeding it is a typed computer-use.timeout.

extraTools.description: Extra binaries `capabilities()` must also probe (a custom target's own tools).
